children: Singapore-based Clifford Capital has priced its ninth public infrastructure asset-backed securities issuance, which at $802.4 million is its biggest program yet.
The infrastructure credit platform said Bayfront IX was two times oversubscribed despite its size, signaling continued investor interest in infrastructure debt.
Bayfront IX comprises 46 project finance and infrastructure loans and bonds across 43 projects in 15 countries and 14 subsectors.
"As investors increasingly seek stable returns, IABS provides access to a diversified portfolio of infrastructure debt they can hold at scale," said Murli Maiya, group chief executive officer.
The securities are rated debt instruments that aim to mobilize private institutional capital into infrastructure.
Bayfront IX offers $762.3 million of senior notes across four classes, and $40.1 million of subordinated perpetual notes.

Asset managers made up the bulk of distribution by investor type, at 56%, followed by banks, and then insurance and pension funds. Geographical distribution was spread across Asia, the Americas and Europe at 45%, 44% and 11%, respectively.
Clifford Capital has issued over $4.8 billion of IABS, financing more than 130 projects, according to its website. Its shareholders include Temasek, ADB and SMBC.
Fitch Ratings earlier affirmed Clifford Capital's AAA rating and stable outlook, citing strong oversight, government support and diversified debt profile.
